hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier MAJOR (round 3): case-twin paths passed both pull_request_target gates with no label while Windows and macOS checkouts hold the twin's text. Real, also for NTFS 8.3 short names, and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced with temporary repos built by plumbing (scratch alias_repro.py: temporary index, core.ignorecase=false, depth-1 fetch of the PR commit into an empty repo, tools run with python -I -S as the gates do). Before the fix, all 6 cases gave rc 0 for adr.py breaker --rev HEAD --base-root, adr.py lint --rev HEAD and check_golden.py --rev HEAD --base-manifest. The cases were governance/invariants.md, decisions/adr-0004-lfu-default-eviction.md (LFU->LRU), tests/Golden/conftest.py, docs/format.md, governance/INVARI~1.MD and governance/decisi~1/ADR-0004-.... git clone on this Windows 11 machine (git 2.45.1.windows.1): the lowercase twin wins; a committed g/INVARI~1.MD overwrote g/INVARIANTS.md; governance/decisi~1/ADR-0004-lfu.md overwrote governance/decisions/ADR-0004-lfu.md ('dir /x' shows DECISI~1 as the short name of decisions). A trailing-dot name is refused by git for Windows (loud failure, not an alias). Fix: new governance/tools/path_aliases.py. It lists every tree entry (ls-tree -r -t -z, git objects only) and reports twins and NTFS 8.3 short-name shapes. Twins are paths equal under one key per component: drop the 16 code points HFS+ ignores, rstrip trailing dots and spaces, then NFD, upper, NFD, casefold, NFD. Short names: up to 6 chars, '~', digits, prefix+digits < 8, optional extension of at most 3, any case. check_golden.py --rev and adr.py --rev (lint, index, breaker, and the --base-rev side) load it from their own directory by path and refuse such a commit anywhere in its tree, with or without --acknowledged: check_golden prints ALIAS lines with exit 1, adr raises AliasError with exit 1. Without the sibling file they exit 2, never pass. Reports are ASCII with backslash escapes. After the fix the same script gives rc 1 for every case and command. Tests: test_gates_refuse_paths_that_alias_on_windows_or_macos runs 9 alias cases through both workflows' own steps (base clone; merge_ref.py --fetch of refs/pull/N/merge from a local origin; judging step with and without the label), plus a clean control (both gates rc 0) and a case-only rename of INVARIANTS.md (no twin; the breaker trips on 'deleted'). Also test_golden_rev_refuses_paths_that_alias, test_adr_rev_refuses_paths_that_alias, test_path_aliases_fold_and_short_names and test_path_aliases_cli_reads_a_commit. Also changed: adr._is_adr_name now accepts ADR- and .md in any case, so lint reports a misspelt adr-0002-d2.md instead of skipping it.

hypotheses_validated.claim: The alias key is at least as coarse as macOS's comparison (NFD + case folding) and as upper-casing (NTFS proxy) for every code point
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Checked over all 1,112,064 non-surrogate code points: whenever NFD(casefold(NFD(c))) or c.upper() is equal for two code points, fold() is equal too. This is asserted in test_path_aliases_fold_and_short_names (about 1.6 s). Named cases: dotless i vs I, sharp s vs SS, long s, Kelvin sign, NFC vs NFD e-acute, U+200C, U+FEFF, trailing dot or space. Exactly the 16 HFS+-ignorable code points in U+2000..U+20FF and U+FEFF vanish; their neighbours (U+200B, U+2010, U+2029, U+202F, U+2069, U+2070, U+FEFE, U+FF00) do not.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier MAJOR: actions/checkout refuses refs/pull/N/merge of fork pull requests under pull_request_target. Real per GitHub's changelog; fixed by not checking the pull request out at all
hypotheses_validated.evidence: github.blog changelog 2026-06-18 (fetched 2026-10-05): checkout refuses fork PR code under pull_request_target when ref matches refs/pull/<n>/merge, and this was backported to all supported major versions on 2026-07-20. The opt-out is allow-unsafe-pr-checkout. Fix: both gates keep a single actions/checkout (the base, ref github.sha). The PR step is now 'python -I -S base/governance/tools/merge_ref.py --fetch "$REPO_URL" --pr "$PR_NUMBER" --merge pr --head "$HEAD_SHA" --base base'. merge_ref.fetch runs git init on a new directory (refuses an existing one). It fetches '+refs/pull/<N>/merge' with --depth=1 --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules and -c transfer.fsckObjects=true. Then update-ref --no-deref HEAD; no working tree is ever written. GITHUB_TOKEN, if set, is sent only as http.<url>.extraheader through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0, never on a command line, with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. URL must be https:// or file://; --pr must be 1-10 digits without a leading 0. Verified against real GitHub, anonymously: actions/setup-python PR 909 fetched (fsck on), merge ref OK ('an ancestor of base'), path_aliases OK on it, 1.8 s, 1.1 MB of objects. Tests: test_merge_ref_fetches_the_merge_commit_as_objects_only covers objects only, shallow, detached HEAD, argv and env per git call, token absent from argv, and git reading the header for the URL and not for another host. It also covers main passing GITHUB_TOKEN, an fsck-failing commit refused (rc 2), and 10 bad-input cases. test_merge_ref_must_be... runs the workflows' own step with fetch (OK, re-run refuses an existing pr/, stale head rc 1). test_golden_and_decision_gates_never_execute_the_pull_request asserts: one checkout; the only ref is github.sha; no refs/pull and no allow-unsafe-pr-checkout in code; exact merge step and env; github.token exactly once.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Upper-casing commutes with canonical decomposition, so the NFD before upper() is redundant
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Hand-made variant dropping it survived the first test set. U+03B1 U+0345 U+0301 and U+03B1 U+0301 U+0345 are canonically equal (one file on macOS), but U+0345 upper-cases to the letter U+0399, which blocks canonical reordering afterwards. Without the inner NFD their folds differ. The pair was added to the twin cases; the variant is now killed.
